nodes.label: Stickman Apple Touch Icon
nodes.rationale: iOS home-screen variant of the stickman mascot on the same opaque navy background; the background is baked in because iOS does not honour transparency for touch icons.

nodes.label: Stickman PWA Icon 192
nodes.rationale: The product mascot: a blue stick figure with an open mouth and one arm raised (mid-speech/presenting pose) on a near-black navy background, with a yellow accent stripe on the torso. This is the app's brand identity — the stickman presenter that the generated marketing videos are built around — rendered at 192px for the PWA manifest.

nodes.label: Stickman PWA Icon 512
nodes.rationale: Same stickman presenter artwork at 512px, the large PWA install/splash size; the figure is drawn edge-to-edge with modest padding, so it is the 'any' purpose icon rather than the maskable one.

nodes.label: Stickman Maskable Icon 512
nodes.rationale: The maskable variant: identical stickman artwork shrunk into the centre with a wide solid navy margin, so Android's circle/squircle adaptive-icon masks can crop the edges without clipping the figure.

nodes.label: File Glyph Icon (SVG)
nodes.rationale: 16x16 monochrome (#666) document-with-folded-corner glyph; a create-next-app default public asset, not Stickman branding.

nodes.label: Globe Glyph Icon (SVG)
nodes.rationale: 16x16 monochrome (#666) wireframe globe with latitude/longitude lines; create-next-app default asset used for external/world links.

nodes.label: Browser Window Glyph Icon (SVG)
nodes.rationale: 16x16 monochrome (#666) application-window frame with three title-bar dots; create-next-app default asset used for 'open in browser' style links.

nodes.label: create-next-app Boilerplate README
nodes.rationale: Untouched scaffolding README from create-next-app (dev server commands, next/font + Geist, Vercel deploy links). It has not been adapted to the Stickman project, so it describes generic Next.js setup rather than this app's pipeline or worker.

nodes.label: Next.js Wordmark (SVG)
nodes.rationale: Black 394x80 'NEXT.js' wordmark logo shipped by create-next-app; framework branding rather than product branding.

nodes.label: Vercel Triangle Logo (SVG)
nodes.rationale: Single white equilateral triangle on a 1155x1000 canvas, the Vercel mark; white fill means it is intended for dark backgrounds.

nodes.label: npm run verify (lint + typecheck + build)
nodes.rationale: A single root-level npm script fans out to both workspaces (web + render-worker) so CI has one gate instead of per-package steps that can drift.

nodes.label: Verify CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs on push and pull_request against master only, pinned to Node 24 with npm cache, so CI matches the Node 24 requirement stated in the root README and catches lint/type/build breakage before merge.

nodes.label: apps/web CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md import)
nodes.rationale: Contains only `@AGENTS.md`, keeping a single source of truth for agent instructions so the Next.js-generated block does not have to be duplicated or manually synchronized.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated and re-added by `next dev` (see node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js). It instructs agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code because this Next.js version has breaking API, convention and file-structure changes versus model training data; in a monorepo the `next` package may not resolve from the repo root, so the docs path is resolved relative to AGENTS.md. Deleting the block from a diff only recreates an uncommitted change, so it should be committed alongside the work.
